subject.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent

question: When `models fallbacks ... --agent <id>` targets an agent that inherits global fallbacks, should it create an agent-local override or mutate the global defaults owner?
rationale: Both designs fit existing internal patterns, but they have different cross-agent effects and source inspection cannot safely choose the permanent public CLI contract.

options.title: Create a local override
options.body: Treat explicit `--agent` as an isolation promise and materialize the named agent's effective model configuration before changing its fallback list.

options.title: Mutate inherited defaults
options.body: Keep the PR's effective-owner behavior and clearly disclose that an agent-scoped command may update every inheriting agent.

options.title: Reject inherited mutation
options.body: Require an existing agent model override before permitting fallback writes with `--agent`.

recommendation.title: Create a local override
recommendation.body: Treat explicit `--agent` as an isolation promise and materialize the named agent's effective model configuration before changing its fallback list.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history signal is on the agent-scope and fallback ownership helpers defining this contract.
